paper.title: Are Stochastic Multi-objective Bandits Harder than Single-objective Bandits?

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic multi-objective multi-armed bandit (MO-MAB) with Pareto regret
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards with Pareto regret are out of scope per the ontology.
unmapped: d-dimensional reward vectors in [0,1]^d; pulling an arm reveals the whole vector

settings.definition_quote: We consider a stochastic multi-objective bandit problem with K arms and d objectives. For each arm a, let Y_{a,1},Y_{a,2},... in [0,1]^d be i.i.d. reward vectors with mean mu_a ... R_T^P := sum_{t=1}^T Delta_{A_t}^P

settings.name_in_paper: Duplicated-coordinate Bernoulli subclass of stochastic MO-MAB (lower bound)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards with Pareto regret are out of scope per the ontology.
unmapped: Reward vector is one Bernoulli sample duplicated across all d coordinates
settings.definition_quote:
Consider the duplicated-coordinate Bernoulli instance
\(
Y_{a,n}=(Z_{a,n},\ldots,Z_{a,n})\in[0,1]^d,
\)
where
\(
Z_{1,n}\sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}\!(\frac12+\Delta_{\mathrm{sc}}),
\qquad
Z_{a,n}\sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}\!(\frac12)
\quad\text{for } a=2,\ldots,K,
\)
and all latent samples are independent across arms and pulls.

symbols.g_dagger: largest objective-wise suboptimality gap max_j g_j (gap between the unique marginal maximizer and the runner-up on objective j)
symbols.Delta_P_max: maximum Pareto suboptimality gap over arms

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Under the stochastic model above, suppose $K\ge 2$, $T\ge K$, rewards are bounded in $[0,1]$, and the instance has positive first-certificate scale $g^\dagger>0$. ... Then Algorithm~\ref{alg:ucb_lcb_guided} satisfies \E[R_T^P] \le K\Delta_{\max}^P + 64 K\log T/g^\dagger + 2Kd\Delta_{\max}^P T^{-2}. In particular, \E[R_T^P]=O(K\log T/g^\dagger).

results.notes: The quantity is expected Pareto regret, defined through the mean-based Pareto gaps, so it is recorded as pseudo_regret. The theorem also states the simplified rate O(K log T / g_dagger).

source.label: cor:certificate_validity
source.quote: Then \Pr(\widehat a_{cert}(T)\neq\emptyset and \widehat a_{cert}(T)\notin A^\star) \le 2Kd\,T^{-3}. Equivalently, with probability at least 1-2KdT^{-3}, every arm accepted by the algorithm is Pareto-optimal.

results.notes: Bounds the probability of certifying a non-Pareto-optimal arm. None of the listed quantities fits, so this is recorded as 'other'.

conditions: Delta_sc in (0,1/4]; arm 1 has mean 1/2+Delta_sc and all other arms have mean 1/2, duplicated across coordinates
the induced scalar policy is uniformly good in the Lai-Robbins sense (regret o(T^alpha) for every Bernoulli mean vector and every alpha>0)

source.label: prop:lower_bound
source.quote:
Assume $K\ge 2$ and fix $\Delta_{\mathrm{sc}} \in (0,1/4]$. Consider the duplicated-coordinate Bernoulli instance
\(
Y_{a,n}=(Z_{a,n},\ldots,Z_{a,n})\in[0,1]^d,
\)
where
\(
Z_{1,n}\sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}\!(\frac12+\Delta_{\mathrm{sc}}),
\qquad
Z_{a,n}\sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}\!(\frac12)
\quad\text{for } a=2,\ldots,K,
\)
and all latent samples are independent across arms and pulls. Suppose moreover that, on this duplicated-coordinate subclass, the induced scalar policy obtained by identifying each observed vector $(Z_{a,n},\ldots,Z_{a,n})$ with its underlying Bernoulli sample $Z_{a,n}$ is uniformly good in the Lai--Robbins sense

results.notes: Delta = Delta_sc, which equals g_dagger and every suboptimal arm's Pareto gap on this instance. The proof uses Lai-Robbins.
